card: Reject empty overflow pages as database corruption in the read-only Berkeley DB parser. When a corrupted BDB wallet contains an overflow page with zero data that links cyclically, parsing loops indefinitely, pinning a CPU core at 100% and hanging wallet migration, wallet dump tools, and node shutdown. The author demonstrates master hanging indefinitely until killed while this PR fails immediately, verified by a new functional test constructing a cyclic BDB file.
changed_since_previous: Rebased with no substantive changes to code or approach.
evidence: PR description benchmarks show bitcoin-wallet dump hanging at 100% CPU for 60 seconds until killed on master, whereas this PR fails immediately with exit code 1
PR description notes migratewallet on master pegs an HTTP worker thread at 100% CPU and leaves bitcoind stop incomplete after 30 seconds
problem: When reading BDB overflow records, the traversal loop terminates only on reaching page 0 or when accumulated data exceeds item_len. An empty overflow page with an hf_offset of 0 adds no bytes to the accumulator, so an empty page linking back to itself or forming a cycle spins indefinitely at 100% CPU, hanging bitcoin-wallet dump, migratewallet RPC workers, and bitcoind shutdown.

risk.why: A false positive check could prevent opening a legacy wallet, but Berkeley DB never writes overflow pages without data.

summary: Reject empty overflow pages as corruption during read-only Berkeley DB parsing in BerkeleyRODatabase::Open. When an overflow page yields no data, the parser throws a runtime error instead of continuing to follow next-page pointers.
